result.summary: This pull request introduces an optional `sat_vb` boolean parameter to the `getmempoolinfo`, `getnetworkinfo`, `estimatesmartfee`, and `estimaterawfee` RPCs. When set to true, fee rate fields are returned in sat/vB rather than BTC/kvB. It adds a `ValueFromFeeRate` helper in `core_io` that formats fee rates with fixed 3-decimal precision using integer division to avoid floating-point rounding errors on sub-1 sat/vB values.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core fee rates are expressed in BTC/kvB across RPC endpoints, whereas users and wallet ecosystems standardly operate in sat/vB. Consumers must perform client-side conversions that risk rounding inaccuracies (especially below 1 sat/vB) and create unnecessary friction for API integrations.
evidence: PR description: 'Returning feerates in BTC/kvB it can be very burdensome and is not good practice, as the most widely adopted units are sat/vB. This PR aims to show a PoC of how we could migrate to sat/vb in a backwards compatible manner.'

PR description: 'Because of sub 1sat/vB environment we cannot rely on GetFee() because it internally uses FeeFrac EvaluateFee() function which rounds the values to always return an int. If the feerate < 1 then it will be rounded to 1 or 0.'
result.scope_notes: For `estimatesmartfee`, adding `sat_vb` as the third parameter shifts the `options` argument from index 2 to index 3 for positional RPC callers, which also affected several functional test invocations.
result.changed_since_previous: The implementation approach remains the same as the previous version; positional argument handling and functional tests were adjusted to accommodate the added parameter index.
result.card: This pull request adds an optional sat_vb boolean parameter to getmempoolinfo, getnetworkinfo, estimatesmartfee, and estimaterawfee, enabling callers to receive fee rates formatted in sat/vB instead of BTC/kvB. It addresses friction and calculation bugs caused by modern wallet software having to convert legacy BTC/kvB rates client-side, especially when handling sub-1 sat/vB rates. Values are formatted via a new fixed-point helper without floating-point conversion. The PR serves as a proof of concept for issue #32093 and has no external dependencies.
uncertainties: The PR description mentions getwalletinfo, but the diff does not modify wallet RPCs.

risk.why: Modifying RPC parameters and fee rate formatting could break client applications that pass positional parameters or expect BTC/kvB formats.
